evidence.AC1: POST /todos with {"title":"past","dueDate":"2020-01-01"} returned 201 with dueDate "2020-01-01". POST without dueDate returned 201 with dueDate null. The date has no time part.
evidence.AC2: PATCH /todos/3 {"dueDate":"2020-05-05"} changed the date. PATCH {"title":...} alone kept the date. PATCH {"dueDate":null} removed it, and the response then showed dueDate null.
evidence.AC3: POST with dueDate "2026-02-30", "21.10.2026", "abc" and "2026-2-3" each returned 400. A numeric dueDate (20260101) also returned 400. PATCH with dueDate "2026-02-30" returned 400.
evidence.AC4: Today is 2026-10-21. I created todos: past-dated and not done; future-dated; without a date; past-dated and then marked done; due today. GET /todos?overdue=true returned only the past-dated, not-done todo. The undated, done, future and due-today todos were excluded. overdue=false returned the other four.
evidence.AC5: In the browser at / each dated todo showed its date in a time element: 2020-01-01, 2099-01-01 and 2026-10-21. The undated todo showed none.
evidence.AC6: On the list page only the past-dated, not-done todo showed the text "überfällig". The future, undated, done-past and due-today todos did not.
evidence.AC7: The page has a checkbox labelled "nur überfällige". Clicking it reduced the list to the single overdue todo ("past").
